scope.current_boundary: Teach the basic assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases, explain the microscopic origin of gas pressure via momentum change and Newton's laws, and derive and use pV = 1/3 N m <c^2> (including 1D collision model and extension to 3D via <c_x^2> = 1/3 <c^2>) and density form p = 1/3 rho <c^2>. Do not pre-teach root-mean-square speed c_rms or the derivation of average translational kinetic energy 1/2 m <c^2> = 3/2 k T.
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of the mole and Avogadro constant from 9702_t15_cm01_l01, and the ideal gas equation of state pV = nRT and pV = NkT from 9702_t15_cm02_l02.
Assumes Newtonian mechanics from Topics 2 and 3: momentum p = mv, rate of change of momentum F = Delta p / Delta t, Newton's third law, and elastic collisions.

immediate_previous.boundary: The equation of state for an ideal gas expressed as pV = nRT and pV = NkT, Boltzmann constant k = R / NA, and thermodynamic temperature T.
can_assume: ideal gas definition: obeys pV = nRT for all p, V, T
macroscopic equation of state pV = nRT and pV = NkT
Kelvin temperature scale T / K = theta / deg C + 273.15

immediate_next.boundary: Root-mean-square speed c_rms = sqrt(<c^2>) and derivation of average translational kinetic energy 1/2 m <c^2> = 3/2 kT by comparing pV = 1/3 N m <c^2> with pV = NkT.
must_not_preteach: definition and calculation of root-mean-square speed c_rms = sqrt(<c^2>)
equating pV = 1/3 N m <c^2> to pV = NkT to deduce 1/2 m <c^2> = 3/2 kT
internal energy of an ideal gas U = 3/2 NkT = 3/2 nRT
